comment: Validation oracles: the published specifications whose own examples are the Prism's test content. tools/oracle/gen.py fetches each source at its pinned SHA-256, takes its examples out mechanically (an example is kept only if every address in it is at a domain reserved for documentation, RFC 2606 and RFC 6761, so no real person's address enters the repository), and reads each one with a reference reader written to the source's own grammar. test/oracle/read.test.mjs then holds the Prism's reading (site/card.mjs readItem) to that reading, field by field: a message's title, sender, time and plain words; an event's title, place and start; a card's name; a header's encoded words as the specification says they display; a base64 test vector as it decodes. Nothing here is invented: a new kind of content is added by naming the specification it follows.

sources.title: RFC 5322 Internet Message Format, Appendix A
RFC 2047 MIME Part Three: Message Header Extensions for Non-ASCII Text, Section 8 Examples
